notes:
- **Your email drafts keep coming on a busy morning.** When two emails arrived close together,
  Archie acted as if it had been switched off: it sent a "While I wasn't running" list and stopped
  writing drafts. Now each email gets its own draft, and that list only comes after Archie has
  really been off for an hour or more. Texts work the same way after a quick restart.
- **Fixed: old due dates coming back after the computer was off.** A reminder that was due while
  the computer was shut, or had lost power, ran late and forgot what it had already told you, so it
  repeated past due dates as if they were new. Now it only mentions what has newly come due.
- **Reminders say what is due, and the month.** "Your Honda's registration expires on October 19",
  not "Registration expires on the 19th". A savings goal whose date has gone by says so, and asks
  whether to set a new date or close it.
- **The morning brief shows when each overdue to-do was due**, and tells you to say which ones are
  already done so your agent can check them off.
- **The last button on your task list says Got it.** It used to say "Leave the list", which looked
  like it would delete your tasks. It never did. Pressing it puts that message away, and anything
  unfinished shows up again on the next list.
- **A power cut is much less likely to cost your agent its memory.** Archie now finishes writing
  each file to the disk before it replaces the old one, so losing power partway through a save no
  longer leaves an empty file behind.
- **Your agent sees more of what you said.** Reports from routines used to fill the recent
  conversation your agent reads, and push your own messages out of it. Only the newest two reports
  stay in it now, and anything pushed out is still checked for things worth remembering. Forget
  this also reaches older memory, so a fact you took out stops coming back.
- **A reply that gets cut off says so.** If your AI company stops answering partway, or the internet
  connection drops, you get the words that already arrived and a line saying what was done and what
  to check.
- **Copy chat** copies the whole conversation as text, and Cmd+A (Ctrl+A on Windows) selects just
  the chat.
- **On a Mac, Archie looks like the rest of macOS 26:** the system font, a sidebar you can see
  through, and the same colors as the iPhone app. The red, yellow and green window buttons come back
  in full screen.
- **The buttons under a message sit together in one bar**, each in its own color, so Send later no
  longer looks like a second Send.
- **The agent page is shorter at the top**, every skill and routine row has its own on switch, and
  jobs say Running, Done, Could not finish or Waiting for you.
- **Settings and Account are down to nine sections, with icons.** You pick a theme from pictures,
  Spending shows bars, and pairing a phone is on an agent's Setup tab, under Chat app, on the
  Archie Mobile row.
- **Archie Mobile can be paired from an Android phone.**
- **Signing in says what is happening at each step**, and the page your browser lands on afterward
  matches light or dark mode.
- **Plainer words on every screen**, in error messages, guides and the store, and in what your agent
  says. Three routines have new names: Daily Briefing is now Today's Calendar, Meeting Sync is
  Meeting Recap, and Meeting Desk Sync is Call Filing.
- New agents start with a shorter, plainer personality. Agents you already have keep theirs.
- New in the store: the **Money at Home** pack. This is Archie; Archie for Business does not carry it.
- Archie opens older Excel files (.xls) and OpenDocument spreadsheets (.ods).
- Catch-up lists show the real time each message arrived, say which inbox when you have two, and put
  whole names on the buttons.
- On Telegram, a question written under a file you send gets answered, and a message that waited
  for the computer to wake up is answered knowing it waited.
- The inbox button on the first run now sets up Email Manager, so the morning check it offers
  actually runs.
